tasks.short: Develop new menus and recipes with the cooks, calculate nutrients and allergens, scale and standardise recipe cards, cost the menu, approve it, and send it to the kitchens.

steps.what: Dietitian develops new menus and recipes with the cooks in the test kitchen
Dietitian calculates nutrients and allergens per recipe in a spreadsheet
Dietitian scales recipes and writes standard recipe cards for recipe standardization
Dietitian costs the menu in a spreadsheet
Dietitian e-mails the new menu to the client kitchens

tasks.design: Recipes are entered once in a recipe system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) linked to a food composition table and the suppliers' product data, so code computes nutrients, the 14 allergens and cost per portion, and scales recipes to any portion count. Standard recipe cards print from the system. Developing and tasting recipes with the cooks and approving the menu stay with the dietitian. Once approved, the menu and cards go to the client kitchens from the system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nutrients, allergens and costs were calculated in spreadsheets for every recipe change.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe systems link food composition and supplier data.
tasks.still_hard: Suppliers change products and allergen data without notice.
tasks.human_edge: Making a low-salt dish that people still enjoy.
tasks.altitude: The dietitian develops and approves instead of calculating.

reach.learn: Whether recipe cards match what is cooked.

evidence.claim: Recipe systems can compute nutrients, allergens and cost per portion from food composition and supplier data.
EU food information rules require the 14 listed allergens to be declared for meals served.

assumptions: Boundary: from the menu brief to the menu released; purchasing is outside.
Input contract: supplier product data loaded; fallback is spreadsheets.
Developing and approving menus stay with the dietitian.
Client kitchens read the menu as before.
research_questions: Do allergen errors on menus fall?

incremental.description: Dietitian checks supplier product changes in the recipe system.

approvals.approved_version: The menu as approved by the dietitian in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few new recipes; high: a full menu cycle with many recipes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find funding calls, plan the program and budget with partners, write the grant proposal, build the budget, check the proposal with partners, and submit it.

steps.what: Dietitian searches funders' websites for funding calls
Dietitian plans the program and budget with partners
Dietitian writes the grant proposal to request program funding

loop.input: The program plan, the call text and earlier proposals of the department.
loop.output: Draft proposal sections in the funder's format.
loop.check: Code checks every assessment criterion in the call is addressed in a section and each section is within the length limits; the dietitian rewrites and approves.
loop.stop: Up to two redrafts per section; then the dietitian writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each call asks different questions; a template does not make the case for this program.

steps.what: Dietitian builds the budget in the funder's spreadsheet
Dietitian checks the final proposal with partners
Dietitian submits the proposal on the funder's portal

tasks.design: Saved searches on the funders' sites send alerts for calls on nutrition topics, so the dietitian does not check websites. A bounded step drafts proposal sections from the program plan, the call text and earlier proposals; code checks every assessment criterion is addressed and sections are within the length limits, and the dietitian rewrites. Budget rates come from the department's standard rates sheet. Planning the program with partners and submitting stay with the dietitian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Calls were found by browsing and proposals written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Funders offer call alerts; language models draft sections that code checks against the call.
tasks.still_hard: Success rates are low whatever the writing.
tasks.human_edge: Building a partnership the funder trusts.
tasks.altitude: The dietitian rewrites drafts instead of writing from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether drafts arrive earlier before the deadline.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft proposal sections; code can check criteria coverage and length limits.

assumptions: Boundary: from the program idea to the proposal submitted; the funder's decision is outside.
Input contract: earlier proposals kept in the department's files; fallback is writing from scratch.
No personal data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much drafted text survives the rewrite?

approvals.approved_version: The proposal as checked with partners in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new topics with no earlier proposals; high: repeat calls with similar proposals.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet designers, builders and equipment suppliers, work out kitchen workflow and equipment needs, review drawings and equipment lists, and track open points.

steps.what: Dietitian confers with design, building and equipment personnel
Dietitian works out kitchen workflow and equipment needs for construction of food service units
Dietitian reviews drawings and equipment lists sent by e-mail
Dietitian tracks open points in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Drawings and equipment lists sit in a shared project space ({PROJECT}) with versions and comments, so the dietitian comments on the current version instead of e-mail attachments. Open points are an issue list in the same space with owner and due date, replacing the spreadsheet. Conferring with designers and defining workflow and equipment needs stay with the dietitian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawings came by e-mail in several versions and open points were tracked in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared project spaces hold versioned drawings and issue lists.
tasks.still_hard: Builders work from their own systems.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a dishwasher in that spot will block the food trolleys.

evidence.claim: Shared project spaces can hold versioned drawings, comments and issue lists.

assumptions: Boundary: from the remodeling plan to open points tracked; construction is outside.
Input contract: designers upload drawings to the shared space; fallback is e-mail.
Conferring and defining needs stay with the dietitian.
research_questions: Are fewer changes needed after construction?

incremental.description: Dietitian keeps the issue list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small refit; high: a new kitchen with many drawing versions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The dietitian keeps developing menus, planning programs with partners and defining kitchen needs; spreadsheet calculations, proposal writing from scratch and e-mail drawings shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A dietitian with more time for menus and programs.
